elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 (unchanged): "Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: § 19.1: "Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications"; § 19.2 as redlined: "For ninety days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: No express duration is stated for the Services/hosted-software conformance warranty in § 19.1 (untimed), and the only stated period is the 90 days now inserted in § 19.2 for Deliverables. Because § 19.2 closes with "after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation," it is ambiguous whether an untimed 12-month-or-longer software warranty survives. No express 12-month software period was added.
§ 19.1 warrants Services performance and conformance with no expiry, which is not less than 90 days; the redline did not disturb § 19.1.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4: "Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."
§ 19.4: "Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the cited or rendered § 19 text (19.1, 19.2, 19.4), and the redline adds none; § 19.3 was not rendered, so its content beyond the malicious-code point cannot be confirmed.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: Per the finding's own rationale, § 19.3's malicious-code warranty is narrowed to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor," which does not warrant that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code; the redline leaves this untouched.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "Services" is defined at § 1.7 to mean "the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services," and § 19.1 expressly warrants that "Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications" with no expiry — i.e., not less than 90 days. Note the redlined operation (§ 19.2, ninety days) reaches Deliverables (reports, configurations, designs; Vendor Technology excluded), not software, so element 1 is in fact carried by § 19.1, not by operation 1. The deterministic period check reads false only because the number is spelled "ninety days" rather than "90"; substantively the period is 90 days.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 warrants professional/workmanlike performance and material conformance of Services with no stated cut-off, exceeding the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4: "Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge," applicable to breach of §§ 19.1 and 19.2.
§ 19.4: "If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it."

reasons: Fallback is complete as rendered: § 19.1 supplies an untimed Services (defined to include the hosted software) and Deliverable conformance warranty plus professional/workmanlike performance, § 19.2 as amended gives Deliverables 90 days, and § 19.4 supplies re-performance/repair/replacement and a refund of Fees paid.

The deterministic 'warranty period ≥ 90 days' check failing is a mechanical artifact: § 19.2 now reads 'For ninety days after delivery,' which is substantively 90 days. Consider rendering it 'ninety (90) days' so the numeral is machine-visible and matches drafting convention elsewhere.

Element-mapping correction for the drafter: operation 1 amends § 19.2, which by § 1.4 covers Deliverables (reports, configurations, designs; Vendor Technology expressly excluded) and not software. Per the software/deliverable boundary, the 'Software … at least 90 days' element is satisfied by § 19.1's untimed Services warranty (Services are defined to include the hosted software), not by the § 19.2 edit. The mapping should be restated as 'already_met' via § 19.1 with operation 1 curing the 15-day extinguishment risk.

Residual operative risk the drafter should consider naming: § 19.2's retained tail 'after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation' is unqualified as to subject matter and, read with § 19.4 (remedies keyed to breach of 'Section 19.1 or 19.2'), could be argued to cut off all correction/refund obligations 90 days after delivery, including for the hosted software warranted in § 19.1. A one-word scoping fix ('after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation for that Deliverable') would remove the ambiguity without adding new obligations; it is not required for fallback completeness but is the only latent inconsistency in the section.

Preferred level is not reached: there is no express 12-month software conformance period, no compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty in the rendered text, and § 19.3's malicious-code warranty is narrowed to code 'intentionally introduced by Vendor.' The rationale correctly notes these as preferred-level points rather than redlining them.

Minimality holds: the sole change is 'fifteen' to 'ninety' in § 19.2. No survival tail, expense language, extra remedies, or boilerplate was added, and the Customer-favourable non-exclusive-remedy sentence in § 19.4 and all of § 19.1 were retained verbatim.

Intent is preserved: no defined term, cross-reference (§ 19.4's references to 19.1 and 19.2 remain valid), timing, or commercial mechanic is disturbed, and the pre-existing § 19.2 cut-off sentence is carried over unchanged rather than newly created.
Margin comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook 90-day floor, and correctly states that §§ 19.1 and 19.4 are unchanged.
